title: Edition Denmark Noksapyeong: A Cafe Inside a Danish Furniture Showroom in Seoul
html:
If you love clean, cozy Scandinavian design, there's a spot in Seoul's Yongsan-gu that mixes a coffee break with a furniture showroom: Edition Denmark Noksapyeong. It's a Danish lifestyle brand's newest space, built as a "shop-in-shop" inside the Noksapyeong store of Fritz Hansen, the famous Danish furniture company. You can browse (and actually sit in) real Danish-designed furniture while sipping tea or coffee — a nice slow-paced stop if you're tired of crowded cafes.

What Is Edition Denmark Noksapyeong?

Edition Denmark is a Seoul-based brand built around Danish design and lifestyle products. Its original showroom-cafe is in Seochon (west of Gyeongbokgung Palace), and the Noksapyeong location is its newer second space, opened on the first floor of Fritz Hansen's Noksapyeong monostore in Yongsan-gu. Rather than a separate building, it's set up as a cafe counter placed right inside the furniture showroom — so the line between "store" and "cafe" is intentionally blurry.

Danish Furniture You Can Actually Sit In

Fritz Hansen is a Danish furniture maker founded in 1872, known worldwide for mid-century modern classics like the Egg Chair and the Series 7 chair — the kind of furniture you've probably seen in design magazines or stylish cafes without knowing the name. At the Noksapyeong space, this isn't a look-but-don't-touch showroom: part of the point is that you can sit at the furniture with your drink, which is a rare chance to properly test out pieces that usually cost a lot more than a coffee.

What to Order: Danish Tea and Coffee

The drink menu leans Danish too. You can get tea from A.C. Perch's, a Danish tea house dating back to 1835 that has historically supplied the Danish royal court, or specialty coffee from Coffee Collective, a well-regarded Copenhagen roaster. If you've already tried Korea's own cafe culture (hand-drip cafes, bingsu spots, and so on — see our Korean Cafe & Dessert Culture guide), this is a chance to try a completely different, Nordic side of the cafe scene without leaving Seoul.

Why Autumn Is a Good Time to Visit

This isn't a place built for a quick caffeine stop — it's built for sitting a while in a quiet, warmly lit room full of wood and leather furniture, which makes it especially pleasant once the weather cools down in fall. If you're already walking around Yongsan-gu or Itaewon on a crisp autumn day, it's an easy, unhurried stop to warm up with tea and look at design pieces you won't find in a typical furniture store.

Good to Know: Location & Hours

Edition Denmark Noksapyeong is at 244 Noksapyeong-daero, Yongsan-gu, Seoul (1st floor), inside the Fritz Hansen Noksapyeong monostore. It's on Noksapyeong-daero itself, within reach of Noksapyeong Station (Seoul Subway Line 6) — check a map app on the day for the exact walking route. It's open Tuesday to Sunday, 10:00–19:00, and closed on Mondays. It's a walk-in cafe with no reservation needed, though seating is limited since it shares space with the furniture showroom, so it can get busy on weekends.

💬 Into Scandinavian design or always hunting for Seoul's quieter cafes? Let us know in the comments — we're always collecting more spots like this.
meta_description: A Danish furniture showroom cafe in Seoul's Noksapyeong: Fritz Hansen pieces, A.C. Perch's tea, and Coffee Collective coffee.
